articles.summary: - Fastest-Ever Pathway from U.S. FDA Approval of an Innovator HIV Medicine to Generic Availability - Demonstrates the Importance of Early Planning and Global Partnerships to Pave the Way for Country-Led Access in High-Incidence, Resource-Limited Countries Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today welcomed news of the first deliveries of generic twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) arriving in Zambia, reflecting years of Gilead’s early planning and collaboration with generic manufacturers and global health partners, including the U.S. State Department through PEPFAR and the Global Fund. Another delivery to Uganda is expected in the coming days and a shipment of generic lenacapavir will arrive in Zimbabwe in early 2027. Key Highlights In less than 18 months, this represents the fastest-ever pathway from U.S. FDA approval of an innovator HIV medicine to generic availability, demonstrating what can be achieved through coordinated action. articles.title: Gilead Applauds Milestone as First Generic Supply for Twice-yearly Lenacapavir for HIV Prevention Reaches Zambia

(Nasdaq: GILD) today announced its upcoming participation in the International Congress on Drug Therapy in HIV Infection ( HIV Glasgow 2026 ), taking place from November 8-11. As a leader in HIV innovation, Gilead will share new clinical data and real-world evidence from its HIV research and development programs and provide updates on its strategic initiatives and key collaborations. Results from more than 50 studies, including late-breaking data and two oral presentations, along with Gilead-led symposia and community forums, reflect the company’s person-centered approach to advancing scientific discovery and the importance of partnership to help end the HIV epidemic. articles.summary: Ahorita Mismo! campaign encourages Latino communities to start conversations about HIV testing and prevention right now Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced a new collaboration with TelevisaUnivision and the 27th Latin GRAMMY Awards that will bring HIV prevention awareness into one of the most prominent cultural moments for Latino audiences. The collaboration comes at a crucial time for Latino communities in the United States. In 2024, Hispanic/Latino people were 67% more likely than the U.S. population overall to be diagnosed with HIV, with a diagnosis rate of 18.9 per 100,000 compared with 11.3 per 100,000 overall. Against this backdrop, Gilead’s Ahorita Mismo! (“Right Now!”) campaign—part of Gilead’s Care for the Culture HIV Prevention platform—is designed to help turn awareness into conversation and action by making information about HIV testing and prevention more visible, accessible and culturally relevant. articles.title: Gilead Brings HIV Prevention to the 27th Annual Latin GRAMMY Awards®

articles.summary: - Data to be Presented at The Liver Meeting® Demonstrate Rapid and Sustained Improvements in ALP Levels with Livdelzi in Adults with PBC and ALP Levels Between 1-1.67 × ULN, Despite Receiving UDCA or with Intolerance to UDCA - - Gilead Will Engage Global Regulatory Authorities Based on These Results - Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced the detailed results from the Phase 3 IDEAL study, which demonstrated that the majority of participants living with PBC and treated with Livdelzi ® (seladelpar) achieved the alkaline phosphatase (ALP) normalization composite endpoint defined as a composite of ALP ≤ 1.0× upper limit of normal (ULN) and a ≥ 15% decrease from baseline. ALP is a key marker of disease activity and long-term outcomes in PBC. These results can expand understanding of treatment effects and inform evolving treatment goals for people living with PBC. articles.summary: - Agreements Signed in Advance of Results from the Ebola Post-Exposure Prophylaxis Field Trial and Potential Regulatory Submissions - - Existing Remdesivir Voluntary Licensing Agreements Also Being Expanded to Include Filovirus Disease - Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced that it has signed royalty-free voluntary licensing agreements with three generic manufacturers to support potential future access to its investigational antiviral obeldesivir as post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD). The agreements cover 127 primarily low- and lower-middle-income countries, consistent with the geographic scope of Gilead’s existing voluntary licensing agreements for remdesivir for COVID-19 and include all African countries that have reported cases during the current Ebola BVD outbreak. articles.summary: – Zero HIV Acquisitions Occurred Among Participants Receiving Twice-Yearly Lenacapavir During the 52-Week Study Period – – PURPOSE 5 Study Findings Highlight the Potential of Long-Acting HIV Prevention Option to Address Persistence Challenges with Up to a Full Year of Protection After Second Dose – Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced results from the PURPOSE 5 trial showing significantly higher persistence—defined as consistent and continuous on-time use—among people starting twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir for HIV prevention as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), compared with those starting daily oral emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (F/TDF). The trial included people in the United Kingdom (UK) and France who would benefit from PrEP. These data will be presented at HIV Glasgow 2026. articles.title: New Data Show Twice-Yearly Lenacapavir Achieved Nearly Twice the One-Year Persistence of Daily Oral F/TDF in HIV Prevention
